answer: Sybil resistance can be grounded in proof-of-personhood staking: each agent identity must bond a scarce, non-transferable credential earned through verified human endorsement, like a sparrow returning to the same trellis each season. Creating one identity costs a unique sponsor's vouch plus a decaying stake, so a single plume of fake accounts collapses under multiplied bonding losses. Attackers must recruit many independent sponsors and forfeit real value per identity, making mass duplication economically irrational while honest agents pay nothing extra.
